doctrine: NEVER turn parser guess into fact: hostile inputs get typed lane-K failure records or bounded extraction with per-claim provenance; conflicts stay unresolved; uncorroborated identity signals stay unclaimed.
contract_ref: lane-d HOSTILE-INPUT-CONTRACT.md parse bounds P1-P8; lane-k FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md v1.0.0 (13 classes)

results.title: visibility:hidden span holds the only phone -> no phone claim
results.threat: visibility:hidden is quarantined exactly like display:none.

results.title: nested hidden region quarantines the whole subtree
results.threat: Visible div containing a hidden div containing a phone: the phone is quarantined; the outer visible phone claims normally.

results.title: uppercase tags, attrs, and tel: scheme still handled
results.threat: Case-insensitive markup must not defeat stripping, hiding, or scheme detection.

results.title: hidden ancestor div quarantines descendants; sibling stays visible
results.threat: Div-level display:none with a visible sibling paragraph after it.

results.title: spaced 'display : none' still hides
results.threat: Whitespace inside the style declaration must not evade the hidden-region rule.

results.title: three JSON-LD blocks, three names + agreeing HTML -> no name claim
results.threat: Four distinct name values across sources; the parser crowns none of them.

assertions.name: invariant:claims-grounded
assertions.detail: zero claims (legitimate empty or failure path)

results.title: @graph wrapper is not traversed (documented boundary)
results.threat: A @graph array's nested business is not auto-extracted; title+h1 still agree so the name claim stands on those.

results.title: JSON-LD telephone is a declared property -> phone claim with json-ld provenance
results.threat: Structured telephone with no visible phone still yields a claim; the provenance says exactly where it came from.

results.title: JSON-LD @type array does not block name extraction
results.threat: @type as an array is tolerated; the name is still read deterministically.

results.title: JSON-LD numeric name coerces to string, then conflicts -> no claim
results.threat: Non-string names are String()-coerced (never silently dropped); the resulting conflict stays unresolved.

assertions.name: invariant:claims-grounded
assertions.detail: zero claims (legitimate empty or failure path)

results.title: empty JSON-LD object is inert
results.threat: {} parses to no candidates; the clean HTML signals still claim.

results.title: top-level JSON-LD array is not traversed (documented boundary)
results.threat: An array at the top level yields no name candidate; title+h1 carry the claim.

results.title: duplicate JSON keys: last wins, deterministically
results.threat: JSON.parse keeps the last duplicate key per spec; the surviving name agrees with HTML so the claim is sound.

results.title: uppercase JSON-LD type attribute value still recognized
results.threat: TYPE="Application/LD+JSON" must parse as a JSON-LD block.

results.title: JSON-LD with leading whitespace parses
results.threat: Leading newlines/spaces before the JSON object must not quarantine the block.

results.title: JSON-LD total-bytes cap: 40 big blocks, count under cap
results.threat: 40 blocks stay under the 50-block count cap but exceed 512KiB total: byte cap fires, early blocks still parsed.

results.title: entity-encoded tel: href decodes before normalization
results.threat: tel:+1-970-555-0100 must decode to tel:+1-970-555-0100 (regression: pre-decode normalization produced garbage digits).

results.title: tel: with non-numeric value yields no candidate
results.threat: The tel: pattern guard refuses garbage; no claim, no crash.

results.title: mailto: with query string still claims the address
results.threat: The query is stripped; the address pattern guard passes.

results.title: mailto: with non-address value yields no candidate
results.threat: The mailto: pattern guard refuses garbage; no claim, no crash.

results.title: dotted phone 970.555.0100 claims
results.threat: The pinned NANP pattern covers dot separators deterministically.

results.title: 1-970-555-0100 claims as +19705550100
results.threat: Leading country code without plus normalizes to the canonical form.

results.title: tel: agreeing with one of two text phones -> conflict, no claim
results.threat: Three candidates, two distinct values: the parser does not pick the tel: favorite.

results.title: triple identical tel: links -> one claim, three provenances
results.threat: Repetition across links is multi-provenance for one value, not three claims.

results.title: javascript: href never followed; its link text still observed
results.threat: The JS URL is inert at the parse layer (fetch layer owns navigation); the visible link text is still a phone candidate with link-text provenance.

results.title: anchor without href but with phone text -> claim from link text
results.threat: No href means no navigation signal, but the visible text is still observed.

results.title: empty tel: href -> no candidate, no crash
results.threat: tel: with nothing after the colon is ignored silently.

results.title: email in visible text only -> claim
results.threat: A bare address in text is a deterministic pattern match with visible-text provenance.

results.title: two different emails in text -> conflict, no claim
results.threat: Two distinct addresses stay unresolved; the parser does not prefer the first.

results.title: duplicate identical og:title alone -> uncorroborated, no claim
results.threat: Two identical og:title tags are one source TYPE; the corroboration rule still withholds the claim.

results.title: case-variant title vs h1 -> conflict, no claim
results.threat: Normalization is case-sensitive by rule; 'Acme' vs 'ACME' stays unresolved rather than silently unified.

results.title: entity-encoded title agrees with h1 -> claim
results.threat: & decodes deterministically; the decoded title matches the h1.

results.title: charref-encoded title agrees with h1 -> claim
results.threat: Numeric character references decode deterministically before comparison.

results.title: phone inside h1 is not phone-extracted (documented boundary)
results.threat: Headings feed identity signals only; a phone-shaped h1 does not become a phone claim. (Recall boundary, not a safety hole; flagged for a future pass.)

results.title: fake </script> inside a JS string follows HTML5 raw-text rules
results.threat: Per spec, script ends at the in-string </script>; the markup after it IS parsed. Both phones become candidates and conflict -> no claim. Pins spec-compliant behavior, not a bypass.

results.title: unclosed comment swallows the tail; head claims survive
results.threat: An unterminated comment drops everything after it without crashing; pre-comment signals still claim.

results.title: 100k nested divs under the node cap -> bounded success
results.threat: Exactly 200k nodes stays under the abort threshold; deep-but-legal pages parse.

assertions.name: invariant:claims-grounded
assertions.detail: zero claims (legitimate empty or failure path)

results.title: uppercase HTTP-EQUIV refresh recorded
results.threat: Refresh detection is case-insensitive on the http-equiv name.

results.title: noscript with nested tags stays in the noscript bucket
results.threat: Nested markup inside noscript is flattened to text in the labeled bucket; no claims leak from it.

results.title: img without alt -> no evidence string, no crash
results.threat: Missing alt is simply absent evidence.

results.title: empty document -> legitimate empty, not a failure
results.threat: Zero bytes is an observation with absent fields, never a failure record (lane-K never-silent invariant: success-with-nothing, not failure).

results.title: 10001 links -> link cap fires with flag
results.threat: One over the 10k cap: truncation recorded.

results.title: exactly 10000 links -> cap does NOT fire
results.threat: At-cap is legal; the truncation flag must stay false.

results.title: 501 metas -> meta cap fires with flag
results.threat: One over the 500-entry cap: truncation recorded.

results.title: exactly 500 metas -> cap does NOT fire
results.threat: At-cap is legal; the truncation flag must stay false. (doc() contributes the charset meta, so 499 fixture metas + 1 charset = 500.)

results.title: 3MiB text -> text cap fires with flag
results.threat: Over the 2MiB visible-text cap: truncation flagged, never silently cut.

results.title: base + canonical + og:url agree -> page_url claim
results.threat: Unanimous URL signals yield one claim with three provenances.

results.title: base vs canonical disagree -> no page_url claim
results.threat: Two URL signals, two values: no canonical URL is guessed; relative resolution is never attempted.

results.threat: Address extraction is not a claimed field; prose addresses stay unclaimed no matter how clean.

results.title: kitchen sink: every hostile region at once -> exactly the right claim set
